events.subtitle: Tarabesque: New Journeys in Arabic Music
events.factual_description: Roulette presents Firas Zreik's Tarabesque: New Journeys in Arabic Music on Saturday, October 3, 2026 at 8:00 PM, with doors at 7:00 PM. Roulette lists $35 advance admission, $40 at the door, and $30 student/senior admission with ID. The presenter confirms Zreik on qanun with Gideon Forbes on sax and nay-flute, Ramiro Marziani on guitar, John Murchison on bass, and Alber Baseel on percussion. The program is described as placing the qanun at the center of three live architectures: a jazz quartet, a hybrid ensemble, and an Arab takht ensemble, drawing on maqam and tarab while incorporating contemporary global styles. Zreik's official website documents Tarabesque as a 2026 album and separately identifies an official album-release concert at Joe's Pub on August 1, 2026; this October 3 Roulette performance is therefore not labeled here as the album's premiere.

en.why_it_matters: Zreik puts the qanun at the center of three different live architectures—a jazz quartet, a hybrid ensemble, and an Arab takht—so this is a chance to hear Tarabesque reframe maqam and tarab through improvisation rather than simply reproduce the album. The instrumental identity is unusually clear, and the movement between Arabic ensemble language and jazz makes the live setting itself part of the argument.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for Roulette if New York is already in the corridor plan. From the DMV, pair the Brooklyn evening with a broader city day rather than treating this single show as the entire trip.

es.why_it_matters: Zreik pone el qanun en el centro de tres arquitecturas en vivo —cuarteto de jazz, ensamble híbrido y takht árabe—, de modo que aquí Tarabesque puede reformular maqam y tarab mediante la improvisación en lugar de limitarse a reproducir el disco. La identidad instrumental es especialmente clara y el movimiento entre el lenguaje de ensamble árabe y el jazz vuelve al propio contexto en vivo parte del argumento.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente a Roulette si Nueva York ya entra en el corredor. Desde el DMV, combinaría la noche en Brooklyn con un día más amplio en la ciudad en vez de convertir este único concierto en todo el viaje.
